verification.fact_verification_explanation: CONFIRMED: The transaction log shows two payments of $110 each, on 2026-06-30 and 2026-07-01, totaling $220 against a single $110 monthly payment. The account note attributes the second payment to a known payment-processor retry issue logged internally on 2026-07-01, so the duplicate withdrawal was our error. NOT CONFIRMED: The customer says the double withdrawal overdrew their checking account. Any overdraft or overdraft fee would be assessed by the customer's own bank, and our records show no overdraft-related charge or link. We cannot confirm or rule out the overdraft from our data.

policy.text:
# Internal Policy: General Dispute Handling Process

**Applies to:** Any complaint not governed more specifically by another policy in this set (i.e., the default process).

## Standard process
1. **Acknowledge** receipt within 3 business days.
2. **Investigate** — compare the customer's claim against account and transaction records.
3. **Classify** the outcome as one of: confirmed (company error), not confirmed (no error found), partially confirmed (mixed), or unable to verify (insufficient data).
4. **Respond** in writing within 15 calendar days of receipt (consistent with standard regulatory complaint-handling expectations), addressing every distinct allegation raised in the complaint individually — a response that addresses only the primary complaint and ignores a secondary request is incomplete.
5. **Close** the case with a documented root-cause category for internal trend reporting.

## What counts as a complete response
- Every distinct factual allegation is addressed (confirmed, not confirmed, or unable to verify).
- Every distinct request the customer made is addressed (a refund request and an account-closure request in the same complaint both need a response, even if only one is granted).
- The response states a clear next step or outcome — never ends on an open-ended "we are looking into it" with no indication of what happens next, unless the case is genuinely still pending additional information.

## What an analyst or agent may say
- May state what was investigated and the outcome in plain language.
- May NOT close a case as "resolved" if any raised allegation was not actually addressed.

## Escalation trigger
Use the dedicated Escalation Criteria policy (document 09) for attorney/regulator/vulnerability triggers. This document covers only the baseline process for complaints that don't meet those triggers.

*This is an internal, generic policy created for a training/demonstration environment and does not reflect any specific company's actual policy.*

draft.draft_text:
You contacted us because your monthly payment was taken from your bank account twice, and because your checking account was overdrawn afterward. We understand how stressful it is to see extra money leave your account and then have to deal with an overdraft.

Here is what we found for each part of your complaint.

Payment taken twice: Our records confirm your payment was taken twice. Two payments of $110 were withdrawn, one on June 30, 2026 and one on July 1, 2026, although only one $110 monthly payment was due.

$220 withdrawn instead of $110: Our records confirm this as well. The $220 is those two $110 payments added together. Our account notes show the second payment came from a payment-processing retry issue on our side.

Overdraft on your checking account: We can't confirm this part from our records. Any overdraft or overdraft fee would be charged by your bank, and we see no overdraft-related charge or link on our side. We can neither confirm nor rule it out with the information we have.

Outcome: Because the second payment was taken in error, we have referred the refund of the duplicate payment for approval. A decision has not been made yet, so we can't tell you the outcome or timing at this point. We will be in touch once the review is complete.

Next steps: You don't need to do anything for the duplicate payment review. If your bank charged you overdraft fees, you're welcome to send us a copy of the statement or notice showing the overdraft and any fees, and we will review it. You can send us any other information at any time by replying to this message, and we will review that too. You are also free to raise this with any other channel you choose.

Case reference: SYN-P02

'Referred for approval' is grounded because the verification confirms the error. The draft also declares the referral in `referral_stated`. The draft does not say any refund has been granted or processed.

verifier.prohibited_language_check: pass — The draft has no apology or fault admission beyond the confirmed fact ('taken in error', 'a payment-processing retry issue on our side'). It makes no guarantee about the future and draws no legal conclusion. It does not discourage other channels, and it says 'You are also free to raise this with any other channel you choose.'
verifier.tone_structure_check: pass — The draft follows Policy 11's order: acknowledgment, findings (one paragraph per allegation), outcome, next steps, then the case reference SYN-P02. It uses plain second-person language and short paragraphs. The extra length is acceptable for a multi-allegation complaint. It has no marketing content.
